tasks.title: Revenue by Customer Segment
tasks.context: Finance wants to know which customer segments generate completed revenue. Customer attributes and order facts live in separate tables.
tasks.goal: Join customers to orders and aggregate completed revenue by segment.
tasks.deliverable: Return segment and total completed revenue, one row per segment.
tasks.prompt: Write the SQL query using customers and orders.
hints: Filter orders to status = completed before interpreting revenue.
JOIN customers c to orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id, then GROUP BY c.segment.
tasks.explanation: The JOIN brings the customer segment onto each order. Filtering removes refunded/cancelled revenue, and GROUP BY segment produces the decision-ready grain.

tasks.title: Large Orders by Status
tasks.context: Operations is reviewing high-value orders of at least 1000. They want counts and revenue totals by status.
tasks.goal: Filter high-value orders and aggregate count and revenue by status.
tasks.deliverable: Return status, order_count and total_revenue for orders with revenue >= 1000.
tasks.prompt: Write the SQL query against orders.
tasks.explanation: WHERE defines the qualifying order population; GROUP BY status then calculates metrics at the status level.
